operational-example.copy: Use Spinner for compact indeterminate loading when an action, field, or inline control is waiting and no progress value exists.

scenario.title: Compact loading states
scenario.meta: Buttons, fields, selects, and inline actions
rationale: Spinner gives compact loading feedback without inventing a percentage.
It can be announced with role status or stay decorative inside a labeled loading control.
Progress Indicator owns measurable progress; Skeleton owns content placeholder structure.

items.rule: SVG circular track for the loading mark.
Uses one semantic SVG stroke for the spinning arc.
Names loading when the spinner stands alone.
Continuous rotation plus a breathing SVG arc communicates waiting rhythm and respects reduced motion.
Maps compact, default, and prominent loading contexts.

items: Use role status with an aria-label when Spinner stands alone.
Use decorative=true or aria-hidden when Spinner appears inside an already labeled loading control.
Do not expose aria-valuenow, aria-valuemax, or percentage text.
Do not rely on Spinner as the only error, empty, or recovery message.

variants.copy: Spinner has one circular indeterminate variant. Size and tone adapt it to field, button, and inline contexts without making it progress.

states.copy: Spinner states describe loading ownership and accessibility mode only. The owner remains responsible for disabled, recovery, completion, and errors.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Spinner does not own completion or error states. Variant remains circular; the owner decides label, disabled state, retry, and recovery.

full-width.copy: Spinner should not stretch. Full-width loading belongs to the owning Button, field, Progress Indicator, or Skeleton region.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use the same compact ring across viewports. Change the owner layout, not the Spinner geometry.

viewport-organization.copy: Spinner stays close to the control or message that owns the wait. Use Skeleton for content regions and Progress Indicator for measurable work.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use small Spinner inside touch-safe loading controls.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use default size for inline status messages with visible copy.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use small or subtle Spinner in dense filters and table controls.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify density, tone, label, and whether Spinner is decorative or announced.

api-foundations.copy: Spinner API exposes label, density, tone, and decorative mode while Design System owns ring SVG geometry, spin rhythm, arc breathing, reduced motion, and accessible loading semantics.

props.name: label
props.notes: Accessible loading label when Spinner stands alone.

props.name: density
props.notes: Maps compact field, default inline, and prominent status density.

props.name: state
props.notes: Explicit loading state for owner state mapping.

props.name: decorative
props.notes: Use when the owning control already communicates loading.

groups.title: Use
items: Use Spinner for compact unknown-duration loading.
Keep it inside the component that owns the wait when possible.
Use a label when Spinner stands alone.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use Spinner for measurable progress.
Do not use it as a full-page placeholder.
Do not keep it after error, empty, or completion state appears.

groups.title: Review
items: Check role status versus decorative mode.
Check whether Progress Indicator or Skeleton is the better owner.

mustTest: Field and select loading consume Spinner
rejectIf: A control uses a custom spinning icon instead of Spinner.
Spinner replaces Skeleton for structured content loading.
Spinner is the only recovery or error message.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Spinner as compact unknown loading. Agents can use it when the owner is clear; humans confirm whether the wait needs progress, structure, recovery, or a larger pattern.
canDecide: Use Spinner for compact unknown loading in fields, buttons, selects, and inline status.
Use decorative mode when the owner already has a loading label or disabled state.
Use Progress Indicator when a value exists and Skeleton when content structure is loading.
mustAsk: The wait can fail, retry, cancel, or block a system.
The loading scope is a page, template, or data region instead of one component.
The system can provide measurable progress.
rejectIf: Spinner is used for measurable progress.
Spinner replaces recovery, empty, or error content.
Spinner appears without an owner or accessible label.
miel.handoff: I am using Spinner for compact unknown loading. Please confirm the owner, label, reduced-motion behavior, and whether this should be Progress Indicator, Skeleton, or a loading pattern instead.
